Armed Conflict & Security
• Russian missile and drone strikes hit multiple Ukrainian regions as leaders gather at the UN; on the Black Sea, a Ukrainian naval drone reportedly sank a Russian kamikaze drone boat. 
• Lithuania’s prime minister said the country is prepared to “fight back” against potential Russian aggression while maintaining evacuation plans amid heightened anxiety. 
• Iranian-linked tensions flared as a senior official suggested Hormuz could reopen within days if a US blockade lifts, while Houthi advances in western Yemen displaced over 100,000 and drew fresh Saudi strikes. 
• Eleven people were wounded in a shooting near a high school in western Turkiye; a suspect was detained. 
• Sri Lanka’s courts are set to deliver verdicts over the 2019 Easter bombings that killed 270, and Australia is probing how F-35 parts en route to the US were diverted to Hong Kong.
Why it matters: Escalating flashpoints from Eastern Europe to the Gulf and Yemen underscore the risk of spillover conflict and maritime disruption, while allied preparedness and defense supply chain integrity are under fresh scrutiny.

Society & Human Rights

• A Venezuelan immigrant allegedly shot by an ICE agent remains detained with a bullet lodged in his back, while a US congresswoman says ICE curtailed her oversight at a Texas facility. 
• A sweeping investigation mapped deaths near the US border’s “virtual wall,” raising questions about surveillance efficacy and rescue response. 
• Berlin’s Left party win energized immigrant communities amid far-right gains; globally, progress toward the 2030 goals on inequality, hunger and education remains far off pace. 
• Academic publishing shifts as hundreds of “diamond” open-access journals begin charging fees.
Why it matters: Democratic norms and human rights—from media freedom to migration enforcement and equitable access to knowledge—are under pressure, with policy and accountability gaps exposed.

Art & Culture.title: Tremaine Emory's ‘Denim Tears from the Pool of Black Genius’ Opens at SCAD Museum of Art
Art & Culture.text: SummarySCAD Museum of Art is staging a retrospective look at Tremaine Emory's practice through his label Denim TearsThe exhibition sets Emory's work against a "Pool of Black Genius" spanning historical and contemporary artistsThe presentation positions his fashion output as a form of conceptual art rooted in the story of the African DiasporaSCAD Museum of Art is turning its focus to Tremaine Emory with Denim Tears from the Pool of Black Genius, a retrospective built around the founder of Denim Tears and his diaspora-driven approach to design. The exhibition traces the breadth of Emory's creative output, treating his self-described "African American sportswear" label as a vehicle for cultural storytelling rather than a straightforward clothing line.The show's organizing idea is the titular "Pool of Black Genius," a framework that situates Emory's work within a wider constellation of influences. To draw that out, the exhibition pulls pieces by Jacob Lawrence, Romare Bearden, Alma Thomas, Faith Ringgold and others from the SCAD Museum of Art Permanent Collection, using them to trace the lineage Emory draws from. It's a deliberate pairing that positions his practice as part of a longer continuum of Black artistic expression rather than a standalone fashion project.Alongside those historical anchors, the presentation devotes significant space to the artists Emory works and thinks in tandem with. Contemporary pieces from collaborators and peers including Arthur Jafa, Hank Willis Thomas and David Hammons round out the display, mapping the network of dialogue that runs through his output. The effect is less a solo survey than a portrait of an artist in conversation, with each collection reflecting another facet of the African Diaspora and the country's complicated shared history.Central to the whole thing is Emory's use of fashion as conceptual art. The exhibition frames his work as a way of translating dense historical references into cultural touchstones, reconfiguring familiar hierarchies and opening up conversations through inclusive gestures. By treating garments as carriers of meaning, the show makes the case that Emory's clothing operates on the same plane as the fine art surrounding it, offering viewers a prompt for reflection and reconsideration.Denim Tears from the Pool of Black Genius, organized by SCAD Museum of Art chief curator Daniel S. Palmer, runs until January 11, 2027 at the SCAD Museum of Art.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.text: SummaryHUF has teamed with anime franchise Evangelion for a Fall 2026 capsule spanning apparel and accessoriesThe lineup pairs the series' imagery with HUF's streetwear sensibility across three T-shirts, a cap and a keychainStandout details include a glow-in-the-dark front print and a six-panel hat that ships with a collectible pinHUF and Neon Genesis Evangelion have joined forces on a new Fall 2026 collection that filters the anime's world through the brand's streetwear lens. Entertainment.title: Aston Martin's Valhalla Spider Is a Rarer Open-Top Version of Its 1,064 HP Mid-Engine Supercar
Entertainment.text: SummaryAston Martin is developing an ultra-exclusive, open-air Spider version of its Valhalla supercar for an anticipated November debutThis new variant will utilize a removable targa top to save weight and preserve the intense dynamics of the original carbon fiber chassisThe drop-top retains the coupe's uncompromised Mercedes-AMG V8 hybrid powertrain, sending 1,064 horsepower to all four wheelsThe British marque is preparing to unleash the Aston Martin Valhalla Spider, an exclusive, open-air iteration of its mid-engine supercar. Anticipated to make its official debut as early as November, the new drop-top represents a rare escalation in the modern exotic landscape. Production numbers for the forthcoming Spider are expected to be remarkably scarce, deliberately undercutting the already stringent allocation of the standard Valhalla Coupe, which is strictly capped at just 999 units worldwide.Introducing an even rarer open-top variant fundamentally shifts the vehicle's footprint in the exotic sector, elevating Aston Martin's standing among the world's most elite car collectors. The standard closed-roof coupe already operates in a highly exclusive market segment, delivering performance metrics that bridge the gap between heavyweights and multi-million dollar flagship hypercars. Removing the roof from the Valhalla amplifies that exclusivity, transforming an already elusive track weapon into a visceral status symbol for the hyper-wealthy.To achieve this open-sky experience, the vehicle will be built around a highly advanced, lightweight carbon fiber monocoque. While this foundational structure provides immense baseline rigidity, the architecture may require targeted additional strengthening to maintain the exact strength and torsional stiffness of the original hardtop model. For the roof itself, the Spider is expected to utilize a completely removable targa top rather than relying on a motorized folding hardtop or a traditional fabric soft top. This manual targa design was chosen specifically to avoid the added weight and mechanical complexity of automated systems, particularly because the supercar lacks the internal storage space required to house bulky folding roof mechanisms.Beneath the sculpted bodywork, the Valhalla Spider will retain the exact powertrain of the standard coupe without any modifications. The core of this hybrid system features a potent, Mercedes-AMG-sourced 4.0-liter twin-turbocharged V8 engine. This aggressive combustion plant works in conjunction with an advanced array of three independent electric motors, mapping two of those motors precisely on the front axle while the third is positioned at the rear. The complex hybrid symphony is mated to a lightning-fast, eight-speed dual-clutch transmission that efficiently routes power directly to all four wheels.When operating at full tilt, the sophisticated all-wheel-drive hybrid system is expected to deliver a combined output of 1,064 horsepower and 810 lb-ft (1,100 Nm) of torque. Crucially, the engineering team's focus on lightweight components and the simplified roof ensures the performance penalties typically associated with convertibles are neutralized. Due to its extensive carbon fiber construction, the Spider is unlikely to weigh more than 3,747 lbs (1,700 kg). This weight management keeps the open-top variant remarkably close to the standard coupe's curb weight of 3,649 lbs (1,655 kg), ensuring the Spider sacrifices virtually nothing in the pursuit of an unfiltered driving experience.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Apple’s New Music Hall Turns a Battersea Power Station Room Into a Full Live-Production Studio
Entertainment.text: SummaryApple has opened Apple Music Hall, a live music venue inside London's Battersea Power StationThe 600-capacity space is engineered so artists can perform, record and film a show all in one placeA 48-speaker spatial sound system and dual mix studios let performances be captured in Spatial Audio and livestreamed worldwideApple Music Hall, Apple's new live music venue in London's Battersea Power Station, is built to function as much like a studio as a concert hall. The 600-capacity room is engineered to let an artist play an intimate set and walk away with a finished recording, a broadcast mix and multicamera video from the same night.The core idea is closing the distance between a small-room show and arena-grade production. Every seat sits close to the performer, but the backend infrastructure is scaled for a touring act, anchored by a 38-foot-wide stage that reconfigures between a traditional front-facing layout and in-the-round setups. Wrapping the audience is a 48-speaker spatial sound system, positioned all around the room so that when an artist performs in spatial, fans hear the set as a fully immersive mix rather than a standard front-of-house feed.Behind the stage, the venue operates as a working production facility. Two dedicated recording and mix studios are built to professional standards, allowing any performance to be captured as a multitrack recording and mixed in Spatial Audio, either live or after the show. The camera side is equally serious: the space is hardwired for 16 or more cameras feeding a purpose-built broadcast control room, with infrastructure that runs iPhone video capture in parallel with traditional broadcast rigs. The net result is a single-show pipeline that outputs a Spatial Audio recording, a broadcast-ready mix and multicamera video at once, with performances also livestreamed globally for fans outside London.The architecture leans into its host building rather than fighting it. Apple Music Hall pulls from Battersea Power Station's design language with heritage brickwork, fluted arches and bronze balconies that echo the structure's historic oriel windows, while a giant glass wall opens up a panoramic view of the concourse and the River Thames beyond. Science & Technology.title: This Digital Radio Gets Messages to the World’s Remotest Locations
Science & Technology.text: Shortwave radios offer a way to connect one location on Earth to practically anywhere else with minimal infrastructure. But these radios come with some drawbacks—a significant one being that, unlike satellite communications, their transmission rates for digital data are typically measured in just hundreds of bits per second. Peter BloomPeter Bloom is the founder of Rhizomatica, a nonprofit that works with remote, indigenous, and off-grid communities around the world to build shortwave and cellular-communication infrastructure. Peter Bloom is the founder of Rhizomatica, a Philadelphia-based nonprofit that has open-sourced a digital shortwave-radio set called the High-frequency Emergency and Rural Multimedia Exchange System, or HERMES. The set operates in the high-frequency (HF) band from 3 to 30 megahertz, as does Mercury, its digital modem. Rhizomatica staff travel around the globe to remote locations in countries like Bangladesh, Brazil, and Ecuador. Wherever they go, they use HERMES to help connect locals to the rest of the world.Bloom spoke with IEEE Spectrum about how HERMES brings better data rates and encryption to shortwave radios.How does HERMES connect remote locations?Peter Bloom: We use the ionosphere as our satellite—or mirror—which helps us move information, voice, and data over really long distances. We’re using small radios that put out about 20 watts of power, and we can pretty reliably do 400- to 600-kilometer links between two radios. We’re talking about places that are not easy to reach, where it’s not simple to put terrestrial infrastructure. What can HERMES send that a basic voice radio can’t?Bloom: HERMES is a software stack—it’s a set of different programs that all work together in order to be able to send data over HF. HERMES allows you to send pretty much any file. Depending on what the file is, whether it’s a photo or an email or a voice memo, it just sends it as a file. It’s like a data pipeline over HF. Why does sending files and data matter more than just voice?Bloom: In emergency situations, people send their latitude and longitude over HF to say, “Hey, I’m here at this place.” People need to be able to send data over HF if there’s a manifest, a parts list, telemedicine—here’s what we have, here’s what we need. Instead of trying to read that out over the air, it’s much easier to just send the file. Same with a photo—if we need evidence that an area was logged illegally, we can just have someone send that over HF, rather than spending days getting down the river to get the photo where it needs to go.Why did you build in encryption that amateur-radio regulations in many countries don’t allow?Bloom: Encryption [regulations] for ham radio operators are different in each country. So it’s all optional—you turn it on, you turn it off. The reason we built the encryption is that some of the partners we work with are in very sensitive areas and don’t want to be sending out information that can be easily captured and used against them.How has HERMES made an impact?Bloom: We’ve been working with artisanal fishers in Bangladesh on a pilot project. There’s 10 or 11 boats that have HERMES systems on them. Pretty soon after we installed those, one of the boats had a mechanical issue in the Bay of Bengal, 100 or 200 kilometers offshore. They were able to send their GPS position and an SOS that they were having trouble. They were able to coordinate the rescue of the crew and the boat. So that was a really cool moment of HERMES in action that we’re super happy about.This article appears in the October 2026 print issue as “Peter Bloom.”

Science & Technology.title: Apple Is Reportedly Developing a Screenless Health Band
Science & Technology.text: SummaryApple’s industrial design team is exploring a screenless fitness tracker band positioned below the Apple Watch SEThe potential hardware pivot follows the September 2026 launch of the data-dense Readiness app for the Series 12 and Ultra 4Health division head Eddy Cue is pushing the stripped-down wearable to accelerate the brand's pace in the fitness categoryApple is preparing a radical shift in its wearable lineup by exploring the development of an Apple screenless health tracker. According to an early August 2026 report from Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, the tech giant’s industrial design team has spent roughly a year conceptualizing new hardware formats. Gurman described this internal exploration as something that transforms the product for a new era, equating the scale of the design rethink to the iPhone eventually jumping to a foldable form factor. The display-free band is being weighed alongside other potential wearable changes such as a round display concept and a ceramic chassis reported by PCMag. However, the reporter noted that the round Apple Watch is unlikely to ever ship, framing the screenless band as the most plausible product to emerge from the initiative. By stripping away the display, Apple could eliminate the daily charging requirements that have long been a common friction point for its smartwatch users while simultaneously targeting a lower price umbrella the brand has never fully occupied just below the Apple Watch SE.While Apple remains uncommitted to the screenless band, and while the device lacks a finalized sensor array, official name, price or release date, the software engine required to power it is already on the market. On September 18, 2026, Apple launched the Readiness app on the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. The system calculates a daily readiness score ranging from 0 to 10 by analyzing recent activity, sleep data and overnight vitals. Users receive one of four daily recommendations: Recover, Pace Yourself, Ready or Go For It. To fuel these insights, the underlying health system samples Heart Rate Variability (HRV) every five minutes. Company officials state this rate is 24 times denser than what the preceding Series 11 could manage. Engineers then split these readings into an overall HRV and a dedicated Recovery HRV, uniquely comparing the data against a user's personal baseline rather than a generic population average.The strongest internal advocate for the stripped-down tracker is Eddy Cue, who assumed oversight of Apple’s health and fitness division from outgoing COO Jeff Williams in late 2025. Cue told colleagues that Apple needs to move much faster in the wearable health and fitness category. His leadership sparked significant internal pivots. Following the management change, Apple deliberately scaled back Mulberry, which was an ambitious AI coaching project. Instead of packaging the intelligence features of the Mulberry project as a premium, paid add-on layer, Apple redirected that architecture directly into the core Health app.By moving advanced AI tracking into the native ecosystem and deploying the intensive Readiness scoring system on current watches, Apple has quietly laid the software groundwork for a display-free future. The screenless band acts as the ultimate hardware vessel for this new infrastructure. Alongside exploring new premium price tiers positioned above the Ultra and Hermès ranges, the potential rollout of a screenless tracker indicates Apple is prepared to heavily segment its wearable lineup to capture every end of the fitness market.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Longevity & Anti-Aging.text: Like many age-related conditions, atherosclerosis is accelerated by the chronic inflammation of aging.
